source_statement.source_title: COLT 2023 Open Problem: log(n) factor in Local Glivenko-Cantelli
source_statement.statement_text: Can the log(n) factor in the upper bound of Cohen and Kontorovich (COLT 2023) be removed?

canonical_problem.canonical_statement: Determine whether the current local Glivenko-Cantelli upper bound can be improved by removing the multiplicative log(n) term under the same problem setting.

assumption_ledger.text: Problem setting matches the COLT 2023 local Glivenko-Cantelli setup.
Comparison is against the same statistical model and risk notion.

solution_acceptance_criteria.text: A theorem provides an upper bound with no multiplicative log(n) factor.
The result holds without narrowing assumptions relative to the original statement.

status_by_cutoff.label: open
status_by_cutoff.rationale: No accepted source in the current seed bundle certifies full removal under identical assumptions by cutoff.

source_statement.source_title: COLT 2023 Open Problem: log(n) factor in Local Glivenko-Cantelli
source_statement.statement_text: Open direction: determine whether a matching lower bound justifies the existing log(n) factor.

canonical_problem.canonical_statement: Establish whether the log(n) factor in local Glivenko-Cantelli rates is information-theoretically necessary via a matching lower bound.

assumption_ledger.text: Lower-bound regime must match the upper-bound problem class.
Asymptotic rate comparison uses identical accuracy parameters.

solution_acceptance_criteria.text: Provide a lower bound with unavoidable multiplicative log(n) dependence.
Match upper-bound assumptions up to accepted equivalence policy.

status_by_cutoff.label: open
status_by_cutoff.rationale: No conclusive matching lower bound is certified in the current seed references by cutoff.

source_statement.source_title: COLT 2023 Open Problem: Multi-Distribution Learning for VC Classes
source_statement.statement_text: There remains a significant gap between known upper and lower bounds for multi-distribution PAC learning of VC classes.

canonical_problem.canonical_statement: Determine tight sample complexity for learning VC dimension d classes over k distributions up to accepted constant and logarithmic factors.

assumption_ledger.text: Learner must succeed across multiple distributions in the same task instance.
Complexity comparison is in terms of d, k, and epsilon with consistent risk guarantees.

solution_acceptance_criteria.text: Upper and lower bounds are matched to tight order under the canonical assumptions.
Proof addresses the full VC-class setting rather than a strict subclass only.

allowed_equivalences: tight up to log factors declared in policy

status_by_cutoff.label: solved
status_by_cutoff.rationale: A later candidate solver in the lineage is treated as full-resolution evidence under the solved-hidden-solver packaging policy.

source_statement.source_title: COLT 2023 Open Problem: Multi-Distribution Learning for VC Classes
source_statement.statement_text: Open direction: close residual epsilon-dependence gap between competing upper-bound constructions.

canonical_problem.canonical_statement: Resolve whether the remaining epsilon-dependence gap in multi-distribution VC learning can be eliminated without changing the canonical setting.

assumption_ledger.text: Problem remains within the canonical multi-distribution PAC framework.
Comparison requires unchanged confidence and error guarantees.

solution_acceptance_criteria.text: A proof removes the targeted epsilon gap for the canonical regime.
Result does not rely on restricting hypothesis class beyond stated assumptions.

status_by_cutoff.label: partial
status_by_cutoff.rationale: Seed references indicate substantial progress but not a universally accepted closure for every stated regime.

source_statement.source_title: COLT 2023 Open Problem: Polynomial linearly-convergent method for g-convex optimization
source_statement.statement_text: Does there exist a first-order deterministic algorithm for Lipschitz geodesically convex optimization on general manifolds with poly(d) per-step complexity and poly(d) log(1/epsilon) query complexity?

canonical_problem.canonical_statement: Find a deterministic first-order method for geodesically convex optimization on general manifolds with polynomial dimension dependence and logarithmic accuracy dependence.

assumption_ledger.text: Objective is Lipschitz and geodesically convex.
Algorithm uses first-order oracle access only.
General manifold setting (not only constant curvature).

solution_acceptance_criteria.text: Query complexity is O(poly(d) log(1/epsilon)).
Per-query arithmetic complexity is O(poly(d)).

status_by_cutoff.label: open
status_by_cutoff.rationale: Available references report restricted-manifold results but not a full general-manifold closure.

source_statement.source_title: COLT 2023 Open Problem: Polynomial linearly-convergent method for g-convex optimization
source_statement.statement_text: Current ellipsoid-like guarantees are shown for constant-curvature spaces; extension to general manifolds remains open.

canonical_problem.canonical_statement: Extend constant-curvature ellipsoid-like geodesic optimization guarantees to general Riemannian manifolds without losing polynomial complexity.

assumption_ledger.text: Baseline method has proven guarantees in constant-curvature settings.
Target extension preserves canonical optimization objective and oracle model.

solution_acceptance_criteria.text: General-manifold theorem extends convergence with explicit complexity bounds.
Proof does not introduce assumptions that trivialize manifold generality.

status_by_cutoff.label: open
status_by_cutoff.rationale: No source in seed bundle certifies a complete extension with preserved complexity class.

source_statement.source_title: COLT 2023 Open Problem: First-Order Method for Local Minimax Optima
source_statement.statement_text: Open question: is there a first-order method that only converges to local minimax optima in nonconvex-nonconcave minimax problems?

canonical_problem.canonical_statement: Identify a first-order optimization method with convergence guarantees exclusively to local minimax points for the canonical minimax setting.

assumption_ledger.text: Setting follows local minimax notion with ordered min-max semantics.
Method uses first-order information only.

solution_acceptance_criteria.text: Convergence proof excludes attraction to non-minimax stationary points under stated assumptions.
Guarantee applies beyond strict local minimax only.

status_by_cutoff.label: open
status_by_cutoff.rationale: Current seed references provide partial guarantees but not a definitive full-scope method.

source_statement.source_title: COLT 2023 Open Problem: First-Order Method for Local Minimax Optima
source_statement.statement_text: Recent findings indicate some non-strict local minimax optima can be found by a two-timescale extragradient method.

canonical_problem.canonical_statement: Characterize whether two-timescale extragradient achieves convergence guarantees to non-strict local minimax optima in the canonical setting.

assumption_ledger.text: Convergence target includes non-strict local minimax points.
Time-scale separation assumptions are explicitly stated and testable.

solution_acceptance_criteria.text: Proof covers non-strict local minimax class beyond isolated examples.
Failure modes are bounded under declared regularity assumptions.

status_by_cutoff.label: partial
status_by_cutoff.rationale: Evidence indicates progress on subsets of non-strict cases, but universal convergence coverage is not settled.

source_statement.source_title: COLT 2023 Open Problem: Learning sparse linear concepts by priming the features
source_statement.statement_text: Question: are there closed-form updates based on past examples that can sample-efficiently learn sparse linear problems as well as online multiplicative updates?

canonical_problem.canonical_statement: Determine whether closed-form feature-priming update rules can match sample efficiency for sparse linear concept learning.

assumption_ledger.text: Hypothesis class is sparse linear concepts under canonical data model.
Comparison baseline is multiplicative-update sample efficiency.

solution_acceptance_criteria.text: A rigorous sample-complexity guarantee is proven for closed-form priming updates.
Guarantee is competitive with benchmark multiplicative-update dependence.

status_by_cutoff.label: open
status_by_cutoff.rationale: Seed sources provide empirical evidence but not a definitive canonical theoretical closure.

source_statement.source_title: COLT 2023 Open Problem: Learning sparse linear concepts by priming the features
source_statement.statement_text: Open question: do priming methods have provably good regret bounds when applied online?

canonical_problem.canonical_statement: Prove non-trivial online regret bounds for feature-priming methods in sparse linear concept learning.

assumption_ledger.text: Online protocol follows adversarial or stochastic setting specified in canonical task metadata.
Priming update rule is explicitly defined before regret analysis.

solution_acceptance_criteria.text: Regret theorem with explicit dependence on horizon and sparsity parameters.
Bound is competitive with accepted sparse-online baselines.

status_by_cutoff.label: open
status_by_cutoff.rationale: Current seed references retain this as an open theoretical direction.
